depends_on: 12-retrieval-neighbour-reuse-gate-2026-10-11 completed with G1 to G3 passing
question: Does asking Clef to choose between the two closest labels, shown with their past examples, keep more correct matches than the neighbour gate alone, still with zero wrong picks?
decision: Whether the production candidate is the neighbour gate alone or the neighbour gate plus the Clef compare check.

H1.statement: The agreement gate passes Tier 1 (W == 0 and C >= 29) and its C is higher than Experiment 12's C on the same 140 cases.

hypotheses.H0: W > 0, or C < 29, or C not higher than Experiment 12's.

decision_rule.pass: H1 holds: agreement gate is the candidate; Tier 2 needs fresh labelled data.
decision_rule.no_gain: W == 0 but C not higher than Experiment 12: drop the Clef step.
decision_rule.unsafe: W > 0: stop this design at cut-off 0.9; do not retune on these cases.

stats.test: Tier 1 rule, then paired count of C against Experiment 12; no significance test
stats.interval: exact one-sided 95% binomial upper bound on W/E

gates.G1_integrity: all pins verify, including Experiment 12 outputs and Clef GGUF and server hashes, before and after
gates.G2_completeness: 280 valid replies, or invalid-reply cases parked and counted as errors
gates.G3_fold_hygiene: prompt examples come only from the case's own outer gallery; an injected leak is refused

reported_not_gated.swap_consistency: share of cases where both orders agree
reported_not_gated.paired_vs_experiment12: both accept, only one accepts, neither accepts

inputs.experiments/12-retrieval-neighbour-reuse: pin by amendment 1 after Experiment 12 completes
pin by amendment 1 after Experiment 12 completes
inputs.experiment12_inputs: all frozen inputs of Experiment 12 plan.json

gate.proposal: label X of the closest same-section gallery member; park if it is none_fit
gate.rival: Y, the next different existing label among the neighbours; park if none
gate.examples: up to 3 members of each label from the case's outer gallery, closest first
gate.accept: order 1 chooses A and order 2 chooses B, each with probability >= 0.9
gate.otherwise: park, including both and neither; never automatic none_fit

clef.question: Which category does the new observation belong with? Compare it with each category's definition and past examples.

choices.A: The new observation belongs with category A.
choices.B: The new observation belongs with category B.
choices.both: The new observation fits both categories equally.
choices.neither: The new observation fits neither category.

clef.scoring: native choice probabilities; temperature 0; no generation
